intro: The language of most smart meters in Europe, Asia and Africa. A meter holds objects: each has a class, a name called an OBIS code, and numbered attributes. A client first opens an association, with a password or with keys, then reads and writes attributes with GET, SET and ACTION.

connect.title: Connect
connect.text: At midnight the head-end opens TCP to port 4059 on the meter. The meter's modem has a private address in the utility's own mobile network (a private APN).

associate.title: Associate
associate.text: Nothing can be read before an association. The AARQ sets the rules (logical names, no ciphering) and carries the password. The AARE accepts and lists the services the meter allows.

value.title: Read the value
value.text: GET reads one attribute of one object, named by its class and OBIS code. The answer is a bare number: 1234567. Its unit is not in it.

scale.title: Read scaler and unit
scale.text: Attribute 3 says what the number means: times 10, in Wh. Now the head-end has the reading: 12 345.67 kWh.

release.title: Release
release.text: The head-end releases the association and closes TCP. The next meter is waiting.

frames.aarq: Let me in: reader client, password 12345678
frames.aare: Accepted. You may use GET, SET and ACTION

notes.tcp: Plain TCP. Port 4059 is registered for DLMS/COSEM. On a serial line or the optical port, the same messages travel in HDLC frames instead of this wrapper.

version.name: Version
version.note: 0x0001: the version of the wrapper. It starts every DLMS message on TCP or UDP.

src-client.name: Source wPort
src-client.note: 0x0011: the client address. This meter was set up to let client 0x11 read, after a password. The public client, 0x10, needs no password but may read little.

dst-meter.name: Destination wPort
dst-meter.note: 0x0001: the management logical device. Every meter has it.

dst-client.name: Destination wPort
dst-client.note: 0x0011: back to the client that asked.

aarq.name: AARQ
aarq.note: Tag 0x60: a request to open an association. 0x36 = 54 bytes follow. This part is BER: a tag, a length, a value.

context.name: Application context
context.note: The object identifier 2.16.756.5.8.1.1: logical-name referencing, no ciphering. With ciphering it would end in .3.

acse-req.name: ACSE requirements
acse-req.note: One bit set: authentication. A password or a challenge follows.

mech-lls.name: Mechanism
mech-lls.note: 2.16.756.5.8.2.1: low-level security (LLS), a password. High-level security (HLS, for example …2.5) sends a random challenge each way instead: each side proves it knows a secret key, which never crosses the wire.

password.name: Password
password.note: Tag 0x80, 8 characters: "12345678". It travels in clear.

user-info.name: User information
user-info.note: Tag 0xBE, then an octet string of 0x0E = 14 bytes with the xDLMS part. Inside it, the coding is A-XDR, not BER.

initiate-req.name: InitiateRequest
initiate-req.note: 0x01, then three options left out (00 00 00): no dedicated key, the default reply mode, no quality of service.

conformance-req.name: Conformance
conformance-req.note: 24 bits, one for each service the client wants to use: GET, SET, ACTION, selective access, block transfer and more.

pdu-client.name: Max PDU size
pdu-client.note: 0xFFFF: the client takes answers of up to 65535 bytes.

aare.name: AARE
aare.note: Tag 0x61: the answer to the AARQ. 0x29 = 41 bytes follow.

diagnostic.name: Diagnostic
diagnostic.note: 0: nothing to report. A wrong password gives result 1 and diagnostic 13, authentication failure.

conformance-resp.name: Conformance
conformance-resp.note: The services the meter allows: GET, SET, ACTION, selective access and block transfer with GET, among others. Only these may be used now.

pdu-meter.name: Max PDU size
pdu-meter.note: 0x01F4: the meter takes messages of up to 500 bytes.

vaa.name: VAA name
vaa.note: 0x0007: the fixed name of an association with logical-name referencing.

invoke-1.name: Invoke ID and priority
invoke-1.note: 0xC1: invoke ID 1, a confirmed service, high priority. The answer carries the same byte.

class-3.name: Class 3
class-3.note: Register: a value with a scaler and a unit.

obis.name: OBIS code
obis.note: 1-0:1.8.0*255: active energy import, all tariffs. Taken apart below.

attr-2.name: Attribute 2
attr-2.note: The value. Attribute 1 of every object is its own OBIS code.

no-selection.name: Selective access
no-selection.note: 0x00: none, send the whole attribute. A load profile uses it to ask for a time range.

invoke-1-resp.name: Invoke ID
invoke-1-resp.note: 0xC1, the same as the request: this answers it.

invoke-2-resp.name: Invoke ID
invoke-2-resp.note: 0xC2: the answer to the second GET.

data.name: Result
data.note: 0x00: data follows. 0x01 would be followed by an error code.

raw.name: Value
raw.note: 0x0012D687 = 1234567, most significant byte first. Without scaler and unit, it means nothing yet.

scaler.name: Scaler
scaler.note: 0x0F: an 8-bit integer. 1: multiply the value by 10 to the power 1.

rlrq.name: RLRQ
rlrq.note: Tag 0x62: release the association. 3 bytes follow.

o-a.name: A · medium
o-a.note: 1: electricity. 6 is heat, 7 gas, 8 cold water. 0 is for objects of no medium, such as the clock.

o-b.name: B · channel
o-b.note: 0: no particular channel. A meter with several inputs numbers them 1, 2 …

o-c.name: C · quantity
o-c.note: 1: active power, import (+P). 2 is export, 32 the voltage of L1.

o-d.name: D · processing
o-d.note: 8: the total over time, so energy. 7 is the value right now.

o-e.name: E · tariff
o-e.note: 0: all tariffs together. 1 and 2 are tariff 1 and tariff 2.

o-f.name: F · billing period
o-f.note: 255: not used, the current value. Other values point to stored billing periods.

facts.transport: TCP or UDP 4059 with a wrapper; HDLC on serial lines and the optical port
facts.security: LLS: a password in clear. HLS: a challenge each way, and AES-GCM-128 for the messages
facts.model: Objects: a class, an OBIS code, numbered attributes and methods

tips: A value without its scaler and unit is not a reading. Read attribute 3 once for each register and keep it: the same 1234567 can be Wh, tens of Wh or kWh.
The client address picks the association, and the association sets the rights. The right password with the wrong client address is still refused.
LLS sends the password in clear. On any network you do not fully control, use HLS and ciphering.
An answer larger than the agreed message size comes in blocks. The client must ask for each next block (GET-Request-Next), or it gets only the first part.

anatomy.obis: The OBIS code of the energy register

playground.file: The head-end's plan for this meter's midnight read: where it is, how to log in, and which objects to read.
playground.client: Client 17 = 0x11, the wPort in every request.
playground.low: Low = LLS: the password from the next line goes in the AARQ, in clear.
playground.clock: Read the clock first. If it is wrong, the load profile's time stamps are wrong too.
playground.register: The register of this lesson: class 3, attribute 2.
playground.keep: Scaler and unit change only when the meter is set up again. Read them once and keep them.
playground.profile: A profile (class 7) with selective access: the meter sends only the rows between the two times.
playground.encoder: DLMS sends numbers most significant byte first (ABCD). Type a value to see the bytes the meter sends.
